html:
Welcome to the official RaggieSoft Backstage companion archive for Katie & Nathaniel.

Because every chapter of Katie & Nathaniel is written strictly in Nathaniel Prairie's first-person point of view, the main novel only shows what Nate and Katie can directly see, hear, and deduce in the moment. Whenever you encounter a Backstage Bonus Feature callout while reading on , you can open these behind-the-scenes dossiers directly inside an in-reader <dialog> modal without breaking narrative immersion.

Behind-the-Scenes Dossiers (2007–2027)

  1. Mar 13, 2007 — The 11:00 PM Curfew Search & Why Locking the Seasonal Closet Door Got Nate and Katie Caught
    Discover how Barton Hall dorm staff tracked Nate and Katie to the Rec Hall without an on-campus sign-out sheet—and why locking a normally unlocked door in a notorious student hookup closet is the exact thing that tipped the night supervisor off while the twins were hidden in the dark.
  2. Mar 14–15, 2007 — How Christopher Vance Scrambled the Dorm Roster & The Thursday Morning Cover-Up
    What happened behind closed doors when Christopher Vance stole an open administrative login to swap opposite-gender dorm room assignments on Wednesday night, why RRC whisked him onto a bus in Staunton at 7:50 AM on Thursday without calling the State Police, and why Nate and Katie's 10:00 AM Level 1 disciplinary counselor meeting never happened.
  3. Feb 2016 — Majority Leader Hawkins's Closed-Door Post-Mortem on HB 663
    What was going through House Majority Leader Richard "Uncle Richard" Hawkins's (R-Danville) and the Speaker of the House's minds during the HB 663 floor implosion—and the four-person pre-floor bill review with Katie and the thirteen-year-old triplet Pages (Sarah, Mandy, and Sam) that Uncle Richard wished the Gentleman from Spotsylvania had done first.
  4. Feb 16, 2027 — Inside Dirksen Room 511: What Was Going Through Commissioner Sterling's and Director Cross's Minds
    Follow the nine stages of bureaucratic panic inside Dirksen Room 511 as DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling and RRC Director Evelyn Cross wonder how a United States Senator knows the exact color of 2007 Level 2 Barton Hall passes, the MedStrip wound-closure strips on a girl's broken nose, and the lumpy bags of curtains inside a Rec Hall storage closet—until the math clicks (41 - 20 = 21) and Governor's Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence reads them the Riot Act from Richmond.
